name: Methane leak detection and repair (LDAR, satellites and continuous monitoring)
aliases: Methane leak detection (OGI cameras, satellites, continuous sensors)
applications: finding and fixing methane leaks at wells, compressors and processing plants
principle: Leaks are located by surveying facilities with optical gas imaging cameras, aircraft or drone sensors, fixed continuous sensors or satellites, and then quantified and repaired. Satellites flag large emission events and recurrent leaks, which are passed to operators for rapid repair. A repeat survey confirms the fix.

performance.metric: fossil-fuel methane emissions that could be avoided at no net cost
performance.basis: about 35 Mt; at average 2024 energy prices; oil and gas share higher than coal

performance.metric: methane emitted by the fossil fuel sector
performance.basis: abatement could have made nearly 100 bcm of gas available

performance.metric: satellites in orbit able to observe methane emissions
share of satellite-detected oil and gas sources that were recurrent
performance.basis: Carbon Mapper analysis of more than 2,000 plumes

costs.metric: greenhouse gas emissions price at which almost all available methane abatement measures across the energy sector would be cost-effective
costs.basis: dollar year not stated; read from the marginal abatement cost curves for methane from the fossil fuel sector, 2024; 1 t methane treated as 30 t CO2-eq (GWP100, IPCC 2021); value of captured methane based on 2024 net-back natural gas import prices; per-survey and per-sensor costs are not stated in the collected documents

source.note: IEA Global Methane Tracker 2025, Overcoming barriers to abatement, p. 42

costs.metric: payback period of many oil and gas methane abatement options
costs.basis: dollar year not stated; document states many abatement options can pay for themselves within a year and around 30% of oil and gas industry emissions could be avoided with measures offering rates of return of more than 25%; value of methane captured based on net-back natural gas import prices in 2024

source.note: IEA Global Methane Tracker 2025, Key findings, p. 12

costs.metric: share of LDAR emissions savings achievable at no net cost to operators (Eurasia oil and gas)
costs.unit: % of LDAR emissions savings in Eurasia
costs.basis: dollar year not stated; includes rapid-response systems for addressing large emissions events detected by satellite

source.note: IEA Global Methane Tracker 2025, Regional insights (Eurasia), p. 55

IEA ETP Clean Energy Technology Guide, dataset of 24 July 2026, 2025 assessment (IEA 1-11 scale): 'Periodic methane emission monitoring in oil and gas facilities' 9; 'Satellite-based methane emission monitoring in oil and gas facilities' 9

advantages: Many measures pay for themselves from the gas recovered
Satellites cover remote and offshore areas
Strong regulatory trend towards required LDAR
limitations: Satellites struggle in overcast and high-latitude regions
Dispersed small sources are a large share of basin emissions

gaps.item: process steps are general practice, not taken from one source
gaps.reason: The tracker names the technologies and measures; the sequence of steps is general knowledge.
